definitions.explanation: The temperature of the surrounding environment, typically around 15-25°C. Frequently used on food labels and in cooking instructions to indicate that something should not be refrigerated.

examples.japanese: バターを{常温|じょうおん}に{戻|もど}す。
examples.english: Bring the butter to room temperature.

examples.japanese: この{薬|くすり}は{常温|じょうおん}で{保管|ほかん}してください。
examples.english: Please store this medicine at room temperature.

examples.japanese: {缶|かん}ビールが{常温|じょうおん}のままだったので、{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: The canned beer was still at room temperature, so I put it in the fridge.

notes:
Very commonly seen on food packaging and product labels. Japanese food labels often specify {常温|じょうおん}{保存|ほぞん} (store at room temperature) versus {要冷蔵|ようれいぞう} (requires refrigeration).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {常温|じょうおん}{保存|ほぞん} (room-temperature storage)
- {常温|じょうおん}に{戻|もど}す (to bring to room temperature)
- {常温|じょうおん}で{保管|ほかん}する (to store at room temperature)
- {常温|じょうおん}の{水|みず} (room-temperature water)
